title: COUSIN_FIELDS
universal_lens: Cousin fields formalize local data patches as sheaf sections over a spatial-temporal lattice. By restricting holonomy to classical operators and utilizing algebraic topology repair classes, the framework unifies distributed consistency with spectral graph approximations, ensuring global coherence without merging distinct underlying state manifolds.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference operates via sheaf cohomology: H0 captures certain answers across overlapping sensor domains, while H1 quantifies measurement inconsistencies. Conformal prediction intervals are derived from spectral Fiedler vectors, providing rigorous block-CRC bounds on uncertainty when gluing disjoint kinematic event streams into a unified probabilistic manifold.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning models game states as constraint satisfaction problems. Surgery-as-IP resolves local tactical conflicts exactly for small subgraphs. Distributed CRDT-like consistency ensures that independent agent state transitions merge deterministically, preventing contradictory play-calls while preserving localized strategic autonomy across the field lattice.

The derivation of cousin fields begins by rejecting naive product expansions of API vocabularies, instead adopting the rigorous gluing axioms of sheaf theory. We define local data patches as sections of a presheaf over a spatial-temporal coverage. The core operator relies on the Mayer-Vietoris sequence to ensure that local observations can be consistently patched into a global state. If the intersection of two patches yields conflicting data, the system does not arbitrarily overwrite; rather, it computes the first cohomology group H^1. A non-trivial H^1 represents a topological obstruction—a 'repair class'—that explicitly flags the inconsistency for downstream resolution. To manage computational complexity, we map these repair classes onto a spectral graph representation. Utilizing the Fiedler vector (the eigenvector corresponding to the second-smallest eigenvalue of the Laplacian), we approximate the minimal cut required to isolate the inconsistent subgraph. This acts as a Block-CRC, verifying the structural integrity of the data manifold. Furthermore, we incorporate concepts from lattice gauge theory, but strictly limit the holonomy to classical operators, avoiding the exponential blowup of quantum-like state spaces. Finally, drawing from database theory and distributed systems, we treat these repaired sections as 'certain answers' akin to CRDTs. The duality lies between the exact, computationally expensive topological repair (valid for small n via surgery-as-IP) and the efficient, approximate spectral validation. Failure modes emerge when the underlying graph disconnects (\lambda_2 \to 0) or when the sheaf obstructions become too dense for localized surgery to resolve, necessitating a complete re-initialization of the coverage.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive lineage traces back to Grothendieck's foundational work on sheaf cohomology in the 1940s, which provided the language for local-to-global principles in algebraic geometry. It intersects with Maxwell's classical electromagnetism, specifically the concept of holonomy in fiber bundles formalized by Ehresmann and later applied to lattice gauge theory by Wilson in the 1970s. The spectral approximation aspect borrows from Cheeger's inequality in the 1970s, linking geometric properties to the Laplacian spectrum. More recently, the integration of CRDTs from distributed computing (2010s) provides the operational semantics for conflict-free merging, grounding abstract topology in practical database consistency models.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: In modeling opposing agents, cousin fields treat each team's tactical formation as a distinct sheaf over the same spatial base. An agent's decision-making process is viewed as attempting to glue its local intent with observed opponent movements. When an opponent executes a feint, it creates a deliberate H^1 obstruction in the defender's perceptual sheaf. The defender's cognitive load is proportional to the complexity of resolving this repair class. The 'theory of mind' emerges from predicting which spectral cuts the opponent will exploit to fragment the defensive graph. Agents do not just react to positions; they anticipate topological vulnerabilities in the opponent's coverage, aiming to induce irreconcilable inconsistencies that force costly surgical repairs.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity vetoes are triggered when the spectral approximation (Fiedler vector) aligns perfectly with a high-dimensional topological obstruction, suggesting a degenerate case where the graph structure offers no discriminative power. Leakage occurs if the 'certain answers' from the database layer prematurely prune valid but noisy sections before the topological repair layer can assess their global coherence. A veto condition is enforced if the classical holonomy restriction is violated by attempting to merge non-commuting state transitions, which would break the CRDT consistency guarantees. Furthermore, if the surgery-as-IP solver exceeds a predefined computational budget for a given subgraph size n, the system vetoes the exact solution and falls back to the documented spectral approximation, ensuring real-time responsiveness over mathematical perfection.
